choice_reason: Physical features improved ordinary and Normal-house errors versus raw. The 4- and 16-member half blends are practically tied; retain the larger internal ensemble to average preprocessing randomness. The half blend improves ordinary and Normal groups more than pure TabPFN, whose all-house advantage is concentrated in the two extremes. This is adaptive selection from historical folds, not independent confirmation.
historical_record_note: The original physical_e16 candidate, its weights, pending-variant flag and timestamp above describe an earlier phase. They are preserved as recorded and are superseded by the subsequent decision below; this was not a preregistered final representation choice.

subsequent_decisions.choice_reason: Equal representation bag improves ordinary and Normal groups versus physical-only half blend while slightly worsening all-house RMSE; use both representations to reduce reliance on exceptional houses.
subsequent_decisions.adaptive_selection_caveat: Model representations and ensemble size were explored on these same historical folds; final bag is informed by those comparisons, not independent validation. No finer bag weight optimization was performed.
phase_history: Initial protocol: raw and bounded physical comparison, 50% total TabPFN / 50% v5.
After raw/e4 and physical/e4 ordinary/Normal benefits, expanded to physical/e16, training-only trimming and quality-category representation.
Initially retained physical/e16 half blend while variant results were pending, as recorded in the original fields above.
After variant comparisons, tested equal representation bag without new CV fits. Compared quality fractions 0, .5 and 1 within the TabPFN half.
Selected equal physical/e16 + quality/e4 representations for better ordinary and Normal scores with a small all-row RMSE cost versus physical-only.

subsequent_decisions.choice_reason: Use a natural equal average of the three distinct predictors. The two-thirds PFN mixture has better ordinary-house and Normal-transaction RMSE than both half and three-quarter PFN mixtures, with more folds improving than three-quarter. This is a discrete natural-weight choice; no continuous or fine-grid weight optimization was performed.
subsequent_decisions.coarse_three_quarter_candidate_role: Diagnostic only; not delivered main weight. Most of its incremental squared-error gain over half comes from the two extreme houses.

subsequent_decisions.selection_caveat: All these representations and weights were compared on reused historical houses and the same folds. The final choice uses those outcomes and carries historical selection bias; it is not new independent validation. Incremental gains from raising PFN above half concentrate in a few houses, even though gains versus v5 remain positive after removing each group's top five improvements.
subsequent_decisions.reproduction_method: Both models were independently reloaded and predicted all 1459 rows for the saved half-weight candidate. Identical component contexts were checked, then those rebuilt predictions were algebraically reweighted to final equal thirds. No new inference was needed for this weight-only update.
